roles.heroLead: A hex-and-subway bath can look 1895 on the surface and be built to 2026 underneath. That's the whole trick in a historic Snohomish home: bonded membrane, sloped base, and a 24-hour flood test we photograph — because the layer nobody sees is the only one that's actually waterproof.
roles.costH2: How much does tile installation cost in Snohomish, WA?
roles.costP1: Snohomish tile projects should budget $14–$26 for each installed square foot — the range spans tile, labor, substrate prep and setting materials, with labor entering at $11/sq ft. Typical marks: tub-shower surrounds near $3,200–$6,800, a 45-square-foot bathroom floor around $900–$1,600, and the complete bathroom — floor, shower, niche — in the $6,500–$14,000 neighborhood.
roles.costP2: Here's what surprises people restoring older houses: the labor follows the layout, not the price tag. A one-inch hex mosaic at $4 a sheet takes more hours to set than $12 large-format porcelain, because every cut and every grout line is paid for in time.
roles.costNote: These bands fit Snohomish-area homes in August 2026, tile and labor and materials combined. Your free estimate produces the written figure — that one is binding, these are orientation.
roles.layersLead: Bottom to top, seven layers. When we open a failed shower in an older house, one of them is missing — nearly always the membrane, skipped once to shave a few hundred dollars, repaid later as a five-figure repair.
roles.whyP1: Leaks keep quiet at first. Moisture slips past grout, works into the substrate, and surfaces a couple of years later as a spongy hallway floor or a water mark on the parlor ceiling. In a century-old frame it travels far before you see it — and the fix by then means framing, subfloor, drywall and new tile.
roles.whyP2: Waterproofing accounts for a tenth or so of a shower build. Leaving it out is the priciest decision a bathroom remodel can make.

roles.faqH2: Tile questions we hear in Snohomish, WA
roles.faqQ1: How much does tile installation cost in Snohomish, WA?
roles.faqA1: Expect $14–$26 per square foot, installed, for tile in Snohomish once you count labor, substrate prep, tile and setting materials — labor by itself begins at $11 per square foot. Standard tub-shower surrounds come in between $3,200 and $6,800; a full bathroom (floor, shower, niche) generally runs $6,500 to $14,000, while a bathroom floor alone — about 45 sq ft — is $900 to $1,600. Format matters more than the tile's sticker price: mosaics and large-format both demand more labor per foot than a plain 12×12.
roles.faqQ2: How much does it cost to tile a shower in Snohomish?
roles.faqA2: For a standard alcove shower in Snohomish, budget $3,200 to $6,800. That number covers demolition, the sloped pan, bonded waterproofing, tile setting, the niche and grout. Benches, curbless entries, steam and full-height stone climb past it. Waterproofing itself is only about a tenth of the total — and it's the tenth that keeps a five-figure failure out of your framing.
roles.faqQ3: Do you waterproof showers before tiling?
roles.faqA3: Always. Behind every shower we set is a bonded waterproofing system built to TCNA methods with an ANSI A118.10 membrane — not bare cement board and thinset. The base goes in pre-sloped, the membrane runs up the walls, corners, seams and pipe penetrations get sealed, and the whole assembly holds a documented 24-hour flood test, photographed, before the first tile is set. Grout and tile shed water; they don't stop it. The membrane is what keeps your framing dry.
roles.faqQ4: How long does a bathroom tile job take?
roles.faqA4: Plan on four to six working days for a Snohomish bathroom. Demolition and dust protection take a day, substrate and waterproofing another — followed by the 24-hour flood test — then one or two days of setting and a final day of grout, silicone and trim. The shower needs another 24 hours for grout to cure before use. A floor by itself is typically a one-to-two-day job.
roles.faqQ5: Porcelain or ceramic tile — which is better?
roles.faqA5: Porcelain, for anything wet or walked on — it's denser than ceramic, chips less, and absorbs under 0.5% water. Ceramic earns its keep on walls and backsplashes, where it costs less and never takes a boot heel. In Snohomish's older homes we get the period look with porcelain hex and subway on floors and shower floors, then let ceramic or glass carry the walls.
roles.faqQ6: Can you install a heated tile floor?
roles.faqA6: Yes — come January in a drafty Victorian, this is the upgrade people phone to thank us for. An electric radiant mat costs $11–$16 for each square foot installed with thermostat, and pencils only while the floor is already open. It rides over an uncoupling membrane, gets resistance-tested twice — ahead of tile and after — and draws its own dedicated circuit.
roles.faqQ7: Do I need to remove the old tile first?
roles.faqA7: Nine times out of ten, yes. Demo and haul-away run from $3.50 per square foot, and pulling the old tile is the only honest look at what's underneath — rot, movement, a subfloor that's seen a century of Snohomish winters — plus it keeps the finished height right at your doorways. Going over existing tile can work on a flat, solid, well-bonded floor, but it buries exactly the problems we'd rather meet at demo than after grout.
roles.faqQ8: How much does a kitchen backsplash cost in Snohomish?
roles.faqA8: For a typical 30 sq ft run, a Snohomish kitchen backsplash lands between $1,100 and $2,200 installed — with trimmed edges, tidy outlet cuts and grout matched to your counters. Expect the high end when the layout gets ambitious: herringbone, mosaic sheets, a framed detail over the range, or slab-look porcelain run full height.
roles.faqQ9: Can you fix cracked tile or regrout instead of replacing?
roles.faqA9: Often — historic houses especially reward it. Repair and regrout open at $8 the square foot, covering stained or powdery grout, one or two impact cracks, and shower corners where grout should give way to silicone. But hollow-ringing tile, loosening that follows a pattern, or a wall that yields under thumb pressure means the substrate itself is gone — patching that merely delays the inevitable. Which situation is yours? We answer that before any quote gets written.
roles.faqQ10: Which Snohomish neighborhoods do you tile?
roles.faqA10: All of Snohomish and the valley around it — the Historic District, Blackmans Lake, Fobes Hill, Kenwanda, Lord Hill, Machias, Three Lakes, Cathcart, Dubuque and Echo Lake — along with Clearview, Maltby and Silver Firs, and neighboring Lake Stevens, Monroe, Mill Creek and Everett. Most of Snohomish County is an easy trip for the crew.
roles.faqQ11: What warranty comes with tile installation?
roles.faqA11: Two years on workmanship from OC Flooring — double what we give carpet, because a tile problem tends to surface in the second year rather than the second week. When we install a waterproofing manufacturer's complete assembly, their coverage stacks on top of ours. And since every shower's membrane and flood test gets photographed, the documentation follows the house — handy when a historic Snohomish home changes hands.
